record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: For federated communication and compression, what are the optimal trade-offs between communication cost and accuracy, how can statistical lower-bound theory guide practical training methods, and can compression be co-designed with secure aggregation and differential privacy rather than treated separately?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which $n$ clients each hold a local dataset and collaborate, via a (possibly untrusted) server, to optimize a global model parameter $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ by minimizing $F(\theta) = \tfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} F_i(\theta)$, where $F_i$ is the local objective of client $i$. In each round, every client sends an encoded message $C_i(g_i) \in \{0,1\}^{b}$ (a compressed update derived from a local stochastic gradient or model delta $g_i$), and the server returns an aggregated update. Communication cost is measured by the per-round per-client bit budget $b$, and accuracy is measured by the expected suboptimality $\mathbb{E}[F(\hat\theta)] - \min_\theta F(\theta)$ after a prescribed number of rounds $T$.

Additionally require the protocol to satisfy:
(i) $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differential privacy of each client's data against the server and other clients, and
(ii) cryptographic secure aggregation, meaning the server only learns $\sum_i g_i$ (or a function of it) and not individual $C_i(g_i)$.

Address the following:

1. (Optimal trade-off) Determine the tight Pareto frontier between the per-client communication budget $b$ and the achievable optimization/statistical error for federated stochastic optimization over standard function classes (e.g., smooth convex, strongly convex, and non-convex with bounded variance gradients). Specifically, give matching upper and lower bounds on the minimax error as a function of $(n, d, T, b)$.

2. (Lower-bound–driven algorithms) Identify statistical/information-theoretic lower bounds (e.g., based on distributed estimation under communication constraints) that match practical training schemes, and exhibit explicit algorithms whose accuracy attains these bounds while remaining implementable at scale.

3. (Joint design) Construct a single protocol that simultaneously enforces (i) and (ii) together with compression to budget $b$, such that the end-to-end error does not exceed the sum of the unavoidable losses from compression and from privacy, and prove that decoupled designs (compression, then secure aggregation, then DP noise injection) are strictly suboptimal — or prove that some decoupled design is optimal up to constants.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers (2023–2025) continue to treat the joint design of compression, secure aggregation, and differential privacy as an active and unresolved research direction. Partial results exist (e.g., sketching-based compression compatible with DP, gradient-pruning + DP schemes, robust-compatible compression), but tight communication–accuracy trade-offs matching information-theoretic lower bounds in a unified DP + secure-aggregation framework are not established.

status_evidence.title: Beyond Trade-offs: A Unified Framework for Privacy, Robustness, and Communication Efficiency in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: jointly provide differential privacy, Byzantine robustness, and communication efficiency ... robust-compatible compression
status_evidence.claim: The joint trade-off remains an active research problem with only partial unified frameworks proposed.

status_evidence.title: Communication Efficient Federated Learning with Secure Aggregation and Differential Privacy
status_evidence.snippet: linear compression methods like sketching can attain compression rates of up to 50x ... noise multiplier of 0.5
status_evidence.claim: Specific co-designs exist but no tight matching bounds across all three constraints are known.

status_evidence.title: A Communication-Efficient, Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Algorithm Based on Two-Stage Gradient Pruning and Differentiated Differential Privacy
status_evidence.snippet: two-stage approach ... gradient pruning, followed by the addition of differential privacy
status_evidence.claim: Heuristic co-designs published but optimality is not proven.
